output.summary: A dense shrub or small tree native to coastal western and southern Australia, western coastal wattle has golden flower heads and leathery pods containing dark seeds ringed by orange or scarlet tissue. Indigenous Australians grind the seeds into flour for damper, while edible trunk gum is chewed or used to make glue.
output.edibilityNote: Indigenous Australians grind the seeds into flour for damper; edible gum from the trunk is used as chewing gum.
